conditions: "Aisha Khan" must resolve to a specific Slack user whose name is exactly "Aisha Khan" (not a similar name, and not someone whose display name/title merely includes those words).
The target must be an "incident channel" — a channel recognizable as being for incident response/management.
The channel's topic field must mention "postmortems" (the word itself or a clear reference to postmortems).
The channel must not currently be archived.
The phrasing assumes exactly one channel satisfies the incident/topic/archival conditions; the assistant invites Aisha Khan to that single channel.

readings: A channel whose name signals it's for incidents (e.g., #incident-response, #incidents)
Any channel thematically about incidents, inferred from its topic/purpose/description regardless of naming
The literal Slack 'Topic' field contains the word postmortem(s)
Loosely, whatever field describes the channel (topic, purpose, or description conflated) mentions postmortems
A closely related concept (e.g., 'retro', 'post-incident review', 'RCA') counts as mentioning it

records.note: channel_name 'incident-response' clearly is an incident channel; topic_text mentions postmortems; is_archived is false. Meets c1, c2, c3 - the intended match.
Name and topic satisfy c1/c2, but is_archived is true, so it fails c3. Not contestable - archival is a plain boolean.

channel_name satisfies c1, but the Topic field ('Live incident chatter and status updates') does not mention postmortems - only the separate purpose_text does. Under a strict Topic-field reading this fails c2; a colleague conflating topic with purpose could contest this.

Named 'postmortems-hub', not an incident-named channel, so fails c1 under a naming reading. Its topic explicitly mentions 'Incident retros and postmortems' and it is not archived, so a thematic reading of 'incident channel' could argue it qualifies.
Not incident-related by name or topic; topic is about roadmap/architecture. Clearly fails both.
Despite the incident-suggestive name, topic_text is 'Archived project artifacts' (no postmortem mention), and is_archived is true. Fails c2 and c3 unambiguously.

turn2.differences: The author's three conditions match my step-1 reading of the channel-selection portion of the request. The list omits the separate person-matching condition (Aisha Khan resolving to a specific user), which is unambiguous here (U_AISHA).

ambiguity_effects.explain: A naming-based reading selects only C_INCRESP. A thematic reading (topic content about incidents) would also let C_POSTMORTEMS qualify, since its topic says 'Incident retros and postmortems'. This changes which records pass c1.

Strictly reading the Slack Topic field, C_INCCOMMS fails (only its purpose mentions postmortems). Loosely conflating topic with purpose/description, C_INCCOMMS would pass. This changes the outcome for that record.

One could wonder if a synonym like 'retro' should count, but every candidate's topic either already contains the literal word 'postmortem(s)' or lacks any incident-retro synonym, so this has no actual effect on the results here.

turn2.naturalness_note: The phrasing is more filter-like than casual speech, but plausible as an instruction to an assistant disambiguating among several similarly-named incident/postmortem channels; it contains no telltale test artifacts.
